item.title: Mazda Zoom-Zoom Stadium: A Carp Baseball Night — Guide
item.description: Mazda Zoom-Zoom Stadium, opened in 2009, is the home of the Hiroshima Toyo Carp and one of the best places in Japan to experience baseball. Uniquely, the Carp are community-owned rather than backed by a single corporate giant, and the bond with the city is fierce: the stands fill with a sea of red, fans chant continuously through their team’s at-bats, and the atmosphere is famously warm and family-friendly. The ballpark itself is an American-style open stadium with wide concourses, a variety of quirky seating including sofa and lie-down seats, and excellent food, including Hiroshima okonomiyaki.

item.title: Tsuwano: The 'Little Kyoto' of the San'in Hills — Guide
item.description: Tsuwano is a small, exquisitely preserved former castle town tucked in a valley in the far west of Shimane, often called a ‘Little Kyoto’ of the San’in region. Its signature is Tonomachi street, where the stone-lined water channels that run alongside the old white-walled samurai houses and merchant storehouses are famously filled with thousands of brightly coloured carp — so many that the fish are said to outnumber the townspeople. Above the town, the ruined stone ramparts of Tsuwano Castle crown a steep hill reached by chairlift, and the whole place has an unhurried, literary atmosphere far from the crowds.
